solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Groups of pupils on top floor? They're highly ranked

definitions.text: Groups of pupils on top floor?
definitions.meaning: whimsically, school forms taught in the rooms upstairs
the social stratum at the top: aristocrats and the wealthy

explanation.surface: A school's senior forms are housed upstairs, and they look down on everyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading takes the phrase literally: classes that meet on the upper storey.
explanation.definitionFit: Society's top tier, the aristocracy and gentry, rank highest in the social order.

clue.text: University official, expert, on cold hill

parts.note: a pro is a professional, an expert
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A university administrator, an expert, stands on a chilly hilltop.
explanation.walkthrough: A tor is a craggy hilltop, a word common in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: At Oxford and Cambridge this officer enforces university discipline.

clue.text: Teen entrant I'm playing for fun

indicators.note: playing about with the letters, as children play, signals they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A teenage newcomer says they are acting just for the fun of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges TEENENTRANTIM; it looks like acting in a show.
explanation.definitionFit: Amusement or diversion: something done for fun is done as a pastime.

clue.text: Lose in court room, small

indicators.note: in says the word Lose sits inside the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: Someone loses their case in a cramped courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'room' looks like part of the court scene, but 'room, small' together is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A cupboard or tiny private chamber is a small room, especially in American usage.

clue.text: For cooking, I have a trout: it's reliable!

indicators.note: cooking a dish mixes its ingredients, so these letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: it's is read as it is, giving IT with is as a link

explanation.surface: A cook vouches for a trout they have to prepare: it's a dependable dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For cooking' rearranges IHAVEATROUTIT; the 's of it's stands for is, linking to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A source deserving trust and backed by expertise is dependable.

clue.text: Well-kept small trading centre

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a mart is a market, a centre for trading

explanation.surface: A tidy little shopping precinct.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat and tidy in appearance, as a well-kept garden or uniform is.

clue.text: Southern judge maybe — a wool-cutter

parts.note: a judge is one who hears cases, a hearer, given as an example by maybe

explanation.surface: A judge from the south who turns out to be a sheep farmer.
explanation.definitionFit: One who shears sheep cuts off their wool.

clue.text: Flower one gentleman brought up

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means the word for gentleman reads from bottom to top

parts.note: sir is the title or form of address for a gentleman

explanation.surface: A gentleman raises a single bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' turns SIR to RIS, since this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden plant with showy blooms, also called flag.

clue.text: Section of kangaroo's trusted sleeping place

indicators.note: Section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of a trusted kangaroo's bedding area.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds settle on a perch for the night, so it is where they sleep.

clue.text: Move faster than exhausted dad near church

parts.note: exhausted, as in used up or spent, means out
pa is an informal word for dad
CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: A worn-out father near a church is overtaken.
explanation.definitionFit: To outstrip someone is to go quicker than them.

clue.text: Release showing prescribed charge to cross river

parts.note: set, as in a set text or set menu, means prescribed

indicators.note: the charge spans the river letter, so R sits inside it

parts.note: a fee is a charge for a service

explanation.surface: A ferry passenger shows the fixed fare for crossing the river and is let go.
explanation.definitionFit: To liberate someone is to let them go.

clue.text: External route revised

indicators.note: a revised version is altered, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of route are the fodder; that the answer also runs on into revised is a coincidence, as revised signals rearrangement

explanation.surface: A ring road has been rerouted.
explanation.definitionFit: Exterior or outside, as an outermost layer is.

clue.text: This guy could become almost radiant

indicators.note: could become says the letters may turn into something else, a rearrangement
almost means the word falls short of its final letter

explanation.surface: A man who could be nearly glowing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims radiant to RADIAN; 'could become' rearranges that.
explanation.definitionFit: A boy's given name, so any man so called could be this guy.

clue.text: Referring to a forward, odious in the extreme

parts.note: a prop is a forward in rugby, one of the front row of the scrum

indicators.note: in the extreme picks the two end letters of the word odious

explanation.surface: Talk about a nasty attacking player.
explanation.walkthrough: A prop is a front-row forward in rugby union and league.
explanation.definitionFit: A preposition meaning with regard to or concerning a subject.

clue.text: Easy catch for model

definitions.meaning: in cricket, a chance so simple a fielder should never drop it
someone who poses for a portrait or photograph

explanation.surface: A model is a simple conquest.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a fielder who drops a gift of a chance has dropped one of these.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a dolly catch in cricket, and one who poses for an artist.

clue.text: Tribune's unusual machine

indicators.note: something unusual is out of the ordinary, so these letters are put in a strange order

parts.note: read as Tribune is, the word Tribune being the letters used

explanation.surface: A newspaper's peculiar printing press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges TRIBUNE; the 's stands for is.
explanation.definitionFit: An engine driven by fluid passing through vanes on a wheel.

clue.text: Subordinate from Virginia upset girl

parts.note: VA is the US postal abbreviation for Virginia

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, reading from bottom to top

parts.note: lass is a word for a girl, common in northern England and Scotland

explanation.surface: An underling from Virginia distresses a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns LASS to SSAL, since this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A feudal tenant owing allegiance to a lord, hence any underling.

clue.text: Italian capitalist?

definitions.meaning: a native of Italy, or of its ancient empire
playfully, a resident of a capital city, here the Italian one

explanation.surface: An Italian who believes in the free market?
explanation.walkthrough: 'capitalist' suggests economics; the question mark flags someone living in the capital, Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of Rome is both Italian and a dweller in Italy's capital.

clue.text: Roam over island for the language?

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means turned over, reading the word backwards

explanation.surface: Should one wander across an island to learn its tongue?
explanation.definitionFit: The Polynesian tongue of New Zealand's indigenous people, an official language there.

clue.text: In German a grammar feature involving rearrangement

indicators.note: In says the answer sits within the words that follow, across their boundaries

explanation.surface: A point of German grammar that involves moving words about.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of German through a into the start of grammar.
explanation.definitionFit: A word play whose letters are reordered; a staple of these puzzles.

clue.text: Gosh! Half of that is fiction!

parts.note: my! is an exclamation of surprise, like gosh!

indicators.note: Half of takes the first two of the four letters of that

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims that half of a story is made up.
explanation.definitionFit: A legend or invented story; also a widely held false belief.

clue.text: Journalists covering Officer Commanding's method

indicators.note: covering says the journalists wrap round the officer

parts.note: the press is journalists collectively
OC is the abbreviation for Officer Commanding; the 's is a possessive link

explanation.surface: Reporters cover how the commanding officer does things.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Officer Commanding is only a possessive joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A series of steps taken to achieve something is a procedure.

clue.text: One far from wise in Djibouti oddly

indicators.note: oddly picks the first, third, fifth and so on letters of in Djibouti

explanation.surface: A fool found in the African state of Djibouti, strangely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' looks like an anagram signal, but it takes the odd letters, and 'in' is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A fool or dimwit is a person lacking any wisdom.

clue.text: Without jackets or coats, eldest shiver unfortunately

indicators.note: things gone unfortunately have gone awry, so these letters are disordered

explanation.surface: The oldest child shivers, having gone out with no coat on.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressed down to one's shirt, with no outer garment on top.
